notes:
Inbound via self-serve signup + support chat. Founder CTO (Maya R.) reached out after trying free tier. Primary ask: hosted API that can do long-context code assist (persisted session up to ~150k tokens) and cheap embeddings for code search.

Key quotes: "we need cheap, predictable per-token economics for code indexing"; "rate limits are killing developer experience — want per-user quotas + graceful 429 handling".

Tech details (from 03/05 call):
- Prototype currently calls OpenAI for code completions and a mix of self-hosted Milvus for vectors. 
- Typical workload: interactive code assistant in IDE + periodic repo indexing. Avg session: 30–60k tokens, spikes to 120k on large workspaces.
- Latency SLO: initial response <600ms for short completions, streaming for multi-line snippets acceptable. Bulk indexing can be async.
- Throughput: ~120 rps at peak for autocomplete; embeddings batch job ~5k files / day.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget; prefer cost predictability over lowest bid.
- Model preferences: open models (Llama2 variants, Mistral-like) but willing to evaluate Redwood-verified options. Careful about hallucination on code.
- SDK asks: first-class TypeScript SDK, example for Vite/Electron plugin, and a Rust client or GRPC example. Also request for native streaming examples and reconnect semantics.

Security/compliance: public cloud OK, but must support SSO/SAML for admin console and audit logs for session activity. No PII in model prompts currently, but may change.

POC ask: 2-week trial with higher burst limits, sample billing estimate for 150k-token sessions, and SDK sample repo.

Notes from AE: engagement warm, founder-engineer duo, quick decision cycle if PoC goes well. Mentioned competitor eval with OpenAI but frustrated by token pricing variability.
